questions.stem: What shape is the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire?

options.text: Concentric circles around the wire
There is no magnetic field around a wire
Radial lines pointing away from the wire
Straight lines parallel to the wire

questions.explanation: A current-carrying wire creates a magnetic field in the form of concentric circles around the wire. The direction of the field depends on the direction of the current.

options.text: A single straight wire carrying current
A permanent magnet shaped like a cylinder
A device that measures magnetic field strength
A coil of wire that produces a magnetic field like a bar magnet when current flows through it

questions.explanation: A solenoid is a coil of wire. When current flows through it, it creates a magnetic field pattern identical to that of a bar magnet, with north and south poles at each end.

questions.stem: Why is soft iron used as the core of an electromagnet rather than steel?

options.text: Because soft iron is easily magnetised and demagnetised, allowing the electromagnet to be switched on and off
Because soft iron is cheaper than steel
Because soft iron is a better electrical conductor
Because soft iron is lighter than steel

questions.explanation: Soft iron is easily magnetised and quickly loses its magnetism when the current is turned off. Steel retains its magnetism, which would prevent the electromagnet from being properly switched off.

questions.stem: Which of the following will NOT increase the strength of an electromagnet?

options.text: Increasing the current
Using a copper core instead of an iron core
Increasing the number of turns of wire
Adding a soft iron core

questions.explanation: Copper is not a magnetic material, so using a copper core would not increase the electromagnet's strength. Only ferromagnetic materials like iron can concentrate the magnetic field lines effectively.

questions.stem: What is the main advantage of an electromagnet over a permanent magnet?

options.text: It never loses its magnetism
It does not require any energy
It can be switched on and off, and its strength can be varied
It is always stronger

questions.explanation: The main advantage of an electromagnet is that it can be switched on and off by controlling the current. Its strength can also be adjusted by varying the current, and its polarity can be reversed.

questions.stem: In the right-hand grip rule for a solenoid, what does the thumb point towards?

options.text: The south pole
The north pole
The direction of current flow
The direction of the magnetic field outside the solenoid

questions.explanation: When using the right-hand grip rule for a solenoid, curl your fingers in the direction of current flow around the coil, and your thumb points towards the north pole of the solenoid.

questions.stem: Why are electromagnets used in scrapyard cranes?

options.text: Because they are lighter than permanent magnets
Because they can pick up all types of metal
Because they do not require electricity
Because they can be switched off to release the scrap metal when needed

questions.explanation: Electromagnets are used in scrapyard cranes because they can be switched on to pick up iron and steel scrap, then switched off to release the load at the desired location. A permanent magnet could not release the scrap.
